quote: Was saying there was no charge. So what why would I need a credit score?
stewart_read: This is a textbook cost/contradiction objection early in the call — exactly the trigger window the schema flags for an inversion flip. Instead of flipping ('what's not free is staying on your current bill') or leading with the bill-swap mechanism, the rep restates the qualifier rule, which reads to the customer as evasive.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have been holding the fuller bill-swap explanation for later in the script sequence rather than skipping it — but the customer's question is direct and answerable immediately, and the rep does eventually give that explanation at 04:38, too late to prevent the first 'not interested.'
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to lead with the bill-swap mechanism the instant a 'free' contradiction surfaces, not after two exit statements. The content existed; the sequencing failed.

quote: I've been in sales my whole life. Okay. I I understand how that works.
stewart_read: The customer explicitly frames himself as sales-savvy and calls out the tactic as manipulative. This is a moment calling for calm, non-defensive de-escalation, but the rep's next line pivots into unrelated equipment specs rather than acknowledging the customer's frame.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep could have been strategically ignoring the callout to avoid amplifying it — but the subsequent pivot to panel branding actively adds new content rather than staying silent on it, undercutting that read.
coaching_implication: When a customer signals sales sophistication and calls out a tactic, the move is transparency, not more pitch. Replay this moment to show the rep how the panel pivot compounded distrust instead of resolving it.

quote: Now what what kind of panels does your company use? We have the we're partnered with Tesla, and we use the all black panels, and they're very pretty. They're very sturdy. They're, like, literally bulletproof
stewart_read: Unprompted equipment-spec content (panel material, durability claims) is closer-tier detail per the schema's scope_creep_signals. It was volunteered mid-objection, when the customer needed reassurance on the credit/free contradiction, not product marketing.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have intended this as a legitimacy builder (Tesla-certified framing) rather than a sales pitch — but the delivery ('very pretty,' 'literally bulletproof') is feature-selling language, not credibility framing, which the schema explicitly flags as an anti-pattern under coaching_philosophy.curiosity_over_features.
coaching_implication: Flag this as a clear scope-creep instance for the 1-on-1 — the rep should redirect equipment questions to 'that's exactly what the specialist walks through' rather than volunteering spec detail unprompted.

quote: It was Tesla's solar panels. Is it Elon Musk ad? It's probably AI. It's probably fake anyways.
stewart_read: The customer names the exact ambiguity the schema anticipates — an ad referencing Tesla/Elon Musk that the customer now suspects is fabricated or a bait-and-switch. The schema provides a canonical reframe ('Tesla referred your inquiry to us — we're their installer partner...') for exactly this trigger, and it was never deployed. The rep's response two lines later pivots straight into panel branding instead of addressing the legitimacy question head-on.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that engaging with the 'is this AI/fake' framing directly would dignify a conspiracy-adjacent claim not worth countering — but staying silent on the legitimacy question while pivoting to product specs left the customer's core suspicion (this whole thing is fake) completely unaddressed, which is the more consequential miss.
coaching_implication: This is the clearest schema-mapped gap on the call: a scripted reframe exists for this exact scam-anxiety/Tesla-legitimacy trigger and the rep skipped straight past it into feature-selling. Replay this exact exchange with the rep — the fix is procedural, not improvisational.

quote: I know. Well, you probably got a script that you're reading off of. So Actually, I I passed that. There's others that do. I don't.
stewart_read: The rep attempts a genuine differentiation move ('I don't read off a script') at the exact moment the customer is disengaging, but the phrasing is halting and undercuts itself given the mechanical qualifier repetition three lines earlier at 03:39.
coaching_implication: The rep has the right instinct here (personalize, differentiate) but the delivery is unpolished and arrives after two objections already handled identically — coach on tightening this line and deploying it earlier, before the objection has repeated.

stewart_read: The call ends with the rep simply complying — "Alright. Thank you. You have a great day." — with no attempt at a final small ask, no acknowledgment of the specific objection, and no next step. This is a full call termination, not a booking failure alone.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer had already said 'not interested' and 'scratch me off your list' twice, continuing to push may have been counterproductive — the polite exit itself may be the correct move under protocols.hello_objection_not_interested's spirit of not arguing a firm no.
coaching_implication: Distinguish for the rep between respecting a firm decline (correct) and having created that decline through earlier mishandling (the actual issue). The exit itself is fine; the four minutes that produced it are the coaching target.
